arxiv-2309-09742.title: Drawing the Same Bounding Box Twice? Coping Noisy Annotations in Object Detection with Repeated Labels
arxiv-2309-09742.creator: David Tschirschwitz, Christian Benz, Morris Florek, Henrik Norderhus, Benno Stein, Volker Rodehorst
arxiv-2309-09742.description: Abstract The reliability of supervised machine learning systems depends on the accuracy and availability of ground truth labels. However, the process of human annotation, being prone to error, introduces the potential for noisy labels, which can impede the practicality of these systems.

arxiv-2407-12259.title: On the Feasibility of In-Context Probing for Data Attribution
arxiv-2407-12259.creator: Cathy Jiao, Weizhen Gao, Aditi Raghunathan, Chenyan Xiong
arxiv-2407-12259.description: Abstract Data attribution methods are used to measure the contribution of training data towards model outputs, and have several important applications in areas such as dataset curation and model interpretability. However, many standard data attribution methods, such as influence functions, utilize model gradients and are computationally expensive.

arxiv-2410-12057.title: Large-scale cloze evaluation reveals that token prediction tasks are neither lexically nor semantically aligned
arxiv-2410-12057.creator: Cassandra L. Jacobs, Loïc Grobol, Alvin Tsang
arxiv-2410-12057.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Cassandra L. Jacobs, Loïc Grobol, Alvin Tsang. In this work we compare the generative behavior at the next token prediction level in several language models by comparing them to human productions in the cloze task. We find that while large models trained for longer are typically better estimators of human productions, but they reliably under-estimate the probabilities of human responses, over-rank rare responses, under-rank top responses, and produce highly distinct semantic spaces.

arxiv-2412-18413.title: Relativistic Dynamics and Electron Transport in Isolated Chiral Molecules
arxiv-2412-18413.creator: Sushant Kumar Behera, Ruggero Sala, Abhirup Roy Karmakar, Matteo Moioli, Rocco Martinazzo, Matteo Cococcioni
arxiv-2412-18413.description: Abstract The Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) effect describes the ability of chiral molecules and crystals to transmit spin-polarized currents, a phenomenon first identified in 1999. Although this effect holds great promise for a broad spectrum of different applications in device physics and synthetic chemistry (including, e.g., spintronics, quantum computing, spin- and enantio-selective chemistry), its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood.

arxiv-2508-17676.title: I Can’t Join, But I Will Send My Agent: Stand-in Enhanced Asynchronous Meetings (SEAM) CCS: Human-centered computing Mixed / augmented reality
arxiv-2508-17676.creator: Zhongyi Bai, Jens Emil Grønbæk, Andrew Irlitti, Jarrod Knibbe, Eduardo Velloso
arxiv-2508-17676.description: Abstract . We propose and explore the user experience of SEAM—Stand-in Enhanced Asynchronous Meetings—virtual reality meetings in which embodied virtual agents represent absent users. During the meeting, attendees can address the agent, and the absent user can later watch the recording from its perspective to respond.

arxiv-2511-01408.title: Leveraging Compact Satellite Embeddings and Graph Neural Networks for Large-Scale Poverty Mapping
arxiv-2511-01408.creator: Markus B. Pettersson, Adel Daoud
arxiv-2511-01408.description: Abstract Accurate, fine-grained poverty maps remain scarce across much of the Global South. While Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) provide high-quality socioeconomic data, their spatial coverage is limited and reported coordinates are randomly displaced for privacy, further reducing their quality. We propose a graph-based approach leveraging low-dimensional AlphaEarth satellite embeddings to predict cluster-level wealth indices across Sub-Saharan Africa.

pmc-11410804.title: SymProFold: Structural prediction of symmetrical biological assemblies
pmc-11410804.creator: Christoph Buhlheller, Theo Sagmeister, Christoph Grininger, Nina Gubensäk, Uwe B Sleytr, Isabel Usón, Tea Pavkov-Keller
pmc-11410804.description: Symmetry in nature often emerges from self-assembly processes and serves a wide range of functions. Cell surface layers (S-layers) form symmetrical lattices on many bacterial and archaeal cells, playing essential roles such as facilitating cell adhesion, evading the immune system, and protecting against environmental stress.

pmc-11475218.title: Exploration of Food Attitudes and Management of Eating Behavior from a Psycho-Nutritional Perspective
pmc-11475218.creator: Anca Mihaela Dicu, Lavinia Denisia Cuc, Dana Rad, Andreea Ioana Rusu, Andrea Feher, Florin Lucian Isac, Daniel Manate, Annamaria Pallag, Florentina Simona Barbu
pmc-11475218.description: Background/Objectives: This study investigates the relationship between food attitudes and the management of eating behavior from a psycho-nutritional perspective, with a focus on the Health Belief Model (HBM). The objective was to explore how emotional food cravings influence different aspects of eating behavior and dietary attitudes, and to identify indirect pathways through which these cravings affect attitudes toward dieting behaviors.

pmc-11590854.creator: Clemente da Silva, Gloria Matambisso, Simone Boene, Eduard Rovira-Vallbona, Arnau Pujol, Kiba Comiche, Antoni Sánchez, Bryan Greenhouse, Arlindo Chidimatembue, Andrés Aranda-Díaz, Paulo Arnaldo, Cristina Ariani, Patrick Walker, Henriques Mbeve, Nelo Ndimande, Dário Tembisse, Shazia Ruybal-Pesántez,

pmc-12609036.title: Der p 23, A Frequent IgE Sensitizer in Humans, Induces Airway Inflammation in Mice
pmc-12609036.creator: Karen Donado, Luis Durango, Inés Benedetti, Nikolina Todorovic, Ronald Regino, Ana Lozano, Victoria Marrugo, Randy Reina, Dilia Mercado, Nathalie Acevedo, Josefina Zakzuk, Enrique Fernández-Caldas, Walter Keller, Leonardo Puerta, Luis Caraballo, Massimo De Martinis
pmc-12609036.description: Der p 23 induces a high-frequency sensitization in allergic individuals. However, its allergenic activity and clinical impact are scarce. We aimed to evaluate the ability of rDer p 23 to induce allergic inflammation in a mouse model and to test IgE reactivity in humans. Female Balb/c mice were sensitized and challenged with rDer p 23 and Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus extract.

pmc-13049075.title: Effect of Pr2O3 addition on the mechanical properties of the mullite/ZTA composites
pmc-13049075.creator: S M Naga, M Awaad, A A Amer, M Arif, M A Saleh, M Elshaer
pmc-13049075.description: To enhance the mechanical and physical properties of Mullite/Zirconia Toughened Alumina (ZTA) composites for advanced engineering applications, rare-earth elements are introduced as dopants. Such composites are characterized by high hardness, fracture toughness, thermal shock resistance, and enhanced physical properties thanks to controlled microstructure through stabilization of the ZrO2 phases, enabling the formation of rod-like particles to enhance mechanical characteristics.

pmc-13086405.creator: Kiran Keswani, Shalini Aggarwal
pmc-13086405.description: Aims:This systematic review aimed to evaluate the influence of storage medium, moisture status, temperature, and duration on the in vitro outcomes of extracted human teeth, including bond strength, microleakage, fracture resistance, and imaging-detected artifacts.Methods:The study is reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guideline.

pmc-13613980.title: Development of a nomogram prediction model for postoperative intra-abdominal hypertension in patients with intra-abdominal infection sepsis based on analgesic drug selection
pmc-13613980.creator: Wenjing Zhao, Guoqiang Chen, Yan Xu, Diyin Yang, Qiaozhen Zhang
pmc-13613980.description: BackgroundPostoperative intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH) is a common complication in patients with sepsis secondary to intra-abdominal infection and is associated with organ dysfunction and prolonged intensive care unit (ICU) stay. This study aimed to identify risk factors for postoperative IAH and develop a nomogram incorporating analgesic strategy and clinical variables for early risk stratification.
